newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa called to open flat to $5 higher.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa called to open flat to $5 higher.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures were called to open unchanged to $5 per tonne higher on Thursday, in a technical correction following three consecutive sessions of losses, traders said.

New York cocoa futures ended sharply lower on Wednesday, pressured by continued speculative liquidation. September cocoa fell $25 per tonne, to $1,458, after ranging between $1,488 and $1,458. December also closed $25 lower, at $1,504, while the back months ended down $24 to $25.
On the charts, traders said September faced resistance near $1,475. Support was seen at $1,450, followed $1,438-$1,436.

London cocoa futures were narrowly mixed early Thursday, after a weak start. At the midday break, LIFFE September was up four stg, to the high of 1,005 stg, after reaching a low of 999 stg. December rose two stg, to 1,034 stg.

Sterling was lower against the U.S. dollar and the German mark after the Bank of England hike rates by 1/4 point to 7.0 percent and signalled they have reached levels consistent with inflation targets.
